claim: Darwinian fitness is a central concept in evolutionary biology.
source: Darwinian fitness is a central concept in evolutionary biology.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific consensus in evolutionary biology.

claim: It is hardly possible to measure fitness for all genotypes in a natural population.
source: In practice, however, it is hardly possible to measure fitness for all genotypes in a natural population.
evidence: This is based on practical limitations in empirical research.

claim: Genetic interactions can often be inferred from fitness rank orders.
source: We demonstrate that genetic interactions can often be inferred from fitness rank orders, where all genotypes are ordered according to fitness, and even from partial fitness orders.
evidence: This is a primary finding demonstrated through theoretical analysis in the manuscript.

claim: The authors provide a complete characterization of rank orders that imply higher order epistasis.
source: We provide a complete characterization of rank orders that imply higher order epistasis.
evidence: This is a theoretical result presented in the manuscript.

claim: The theory applies to all common types of gene interactions.
source: Our theory applies to all common types of gene interactions and facilitates comprehensive investigations of diverse genetic interactions.
evidence: This is a claim about the generality of the theoretical framework developed.

claim: Higher order interactions among mutations were revealed in HIV-1 genetic systems.
source: We analyzed various genetic systems comprising HIV-1, the malaria-causing parasite Plasmodium vivax, the fungus Aspergillus niger, and the TEM-family of β-lactamase associated with antibiotic resistance. For all systems, our approach revealed higher order interactions among mutations.
evidence: This is an empirical finding from applying the method to HIV-1 data.

claim: Higher order interactions among mutations were revealed in Plasmodium vivax genetic systems.
source: We analyzed various genetic systems comprising HIV-1, the malaria-causing parasite Plasmodium vivax, the fungus Aspergillus niger, and the TEM-family of β-lactamase associated with antibiotic resistance. For all systems, our approach revealed higher order interactions among mutations.
evidence: This is an empirical finding from applying the method to Plasmodium vivax data.

claim: Higher order interactions among mutations were revealed in Aspergillus niger genetic systems.
source: We analyzed various genetic systems comprising HIV-1, the malaria-causing parasite Plasmodium vivax, the fungus Aspergillus niger, and the TEM-family of β-lactamase associated with antibiotic resistance. For all systems, our approach revealed higher order interactions among mutations.
evidence: This is an empirical finding from applying the method to Aspergillus niger data.

claim: Higher order interactions among mutations were revealed in TEM-family β-lactamase genetic systems.
source: We analyzed various genetic systems comprising HIV-1, the malaria-causing parasite Plasmodium vivax, the fungus Aspergillus niger, and the TEM-family of β-lactamase associated with antibiotic resistance. For all systems, our approach revealed higher order interactions among mutations.
evidence: This is an empirical finding from applying the method to β-lactamase data.

claim: The fitness landscape is the collection of all fitness values for all genotypes.
source: The collection of all fitness values for all genotypes, referred to as the fitness landscape, is a central concept in evolutionary biology (Wright, 1932; Orr, 2009).
evidence: This is a definition supported by citations to foundational work.

claim: The fitness landscape can have a strong impact on the fate of the evolving population.
source: The fitness landscape can have a strong impact on the fate of the evolving population, such as, for example, the risk of a pathogen population to develop drug resistance and to survive under drug treatment (de Visser and Krug, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to relevant literature.

claim: Genetic interactions, or epistasis, are abundant in nature.
source: Genetic interactions, or epistasis, are abundant in nature.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge.

claim: Unless there are genetic interactions, fitness is assumed to be additive.
source: Unless there are genetic interactions, we assume that fitness is additive, that is, the fitness effects of individual mutations sum.
evidence: This is a theoretical assumption used in the framework.

claim: An additive fitness landscape is determined by the wild-type and single-mutant fitness values.
source: An additive fitness landscape is determined by the wild-type and single-mutant fitness values.
evidence: This is a mathematical property of additive landscapes.

claim: If the fitness landscape is determined by the wild-type, single-mutant, and double-mutant fitness values, then it has no higher order epistasis.
source: If the fitness landscape is determined by the wild-type, single-mutant, and double-mutant fitness values, then we say that it has no higher order epistasis.
evidence: This is a definition used in the theoretical framework.

claim: Higher order epistasis means that the fitness of a multiple mutant is unexpected given the fitness of the wild type and all single and double mutants.
source: Intuitively, higher order epistasis means that the fitness of a multiple mutant is unexpected given the fitness of the wild type and all single and double mutants.
evidence: This is an intuitive explanation of the concept.

claim: Weinreich et al. (2006) showed that five mutations jointly increase antibiotic resistance considerably more than expected.
source: For example, Weinreich et al. (2006) showed that five mutations jointly increase antibiotic resistance considerably more than expected.
evidence: This is supported by citation to the referenced study.

claim: Measuring fitness experimentally is challenging.
source: Measuring fitness experimentally is challenging.
evidence: This is a statement about practical limitations in experimental biology.

claim: Fitness measurements tend to come with high uncertainty.
source: Fitness measurements tend to come with high uncertainty and they are often obtained only for a subset of genotypes.
evidence: This is based on practical experience in empirical research.

claim: Fitness measurements are often obtained only for a subset of genotypes.
source: Fitness measurements tend to come with high uncertainty and they are often obtained only for a subset of genotypes.
evidence: This is based on practical limitations in experimental design.

claim: Fitness can sometimes not be measured directly at all.
source: Moreover, fitness can sometimes not be measured directly at all.
evidence: This is a statement about practical limitations in measuring fitness.

claim: Phenotypes that approximate fitness well are sometimes considered instead of direct fitness measurements.
source: Instead, phenotypes are considered that can be measured and are believed to approximate fitness well.
evidence: This is a common practice in empirical research.

claim: Antimicrobial drug resistance is the dominating survival factor for a bacterial population under drug exposure.
source: For instance, antimicrobial drug resistance is the dominating survival factor for a bacterial population under drug exposure, so that the degree of resistance is a good substitute measure of fitness.
evidence: This is based on biological understanding of bacterial populations under drug selection.

claim: The degree of resistance is a good substitute measure of fitness for bacterial populations under drug exposure.
source: For instance, antimicrobial drug resistance is the dominating survival factor for a bacterial population under drug exposure, so that the degree of resistance is a good substitute measure of fitness.
evidence: This is an inference based on the relationship between resistance and survival.

claim: Presence or absence of epistasis in proxy data does not generally imply presence or absence of epistasis in the fitness landscape itself.
source: Although it is possible to study epistasis of the proxy data, in general, presence or absence of epistasis in the proxy landscape does not imply presence or absence of epistasis in the fitness landscape itself.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the relationship between proxy measures and actual fitness.

claim: Epistatic interactions have been measured experimentally in E. coli.
source: Experimentally, epistatic interactions have been measured in several genetic systems, including E. coli (Khan et al., 2011; Weinreich et al., 2006; Poelwijk et al., 2007), HIV-1 (da Silva et al., 2010; Segal et al., 2004), and other viruses (Wylie and Shakhnovich, 2011; Sanjuán, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to empirical studies.

claim: Epistatic interactions have been measured experimentally in HIV-1.
source: Experimentally, epistatic interactions have been measured in several genetic systems, including E. coli (Khan et al., 2011; Weinreich et al., 2006; Poelwijk et al., 2007), HIV-1 (da Silva et al., 2010; Segal et al., 2004), and other viruses (Wylie and Shakhnovich, 2011; Sanjuán, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to empirical studies.

claim: Epistatic interactions have been measured experimentally in other viruses.
source: Experimentally, epistatic interactions have been measured in several genetic systems, including E. coli (Khan et al., 2011; Weinreich et al., 2006; Poelwijk et al., 2007), HIV-1 (da Silva et al., 2010; Segal et al., 2004), and other viruses (Wylie and Shakhnovich, 2011; Sanjuán, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to empirical studies.

claim: Studies of epistasis involve the analysis of standing genetic variation or spontaneous mutations.
source: These and similar studies involve the analysis of standing genetic variation or spontaneous mutations (Bonhoeffer et al., 2004; Bershtein et al., 2006), engineered site-directed mutations (Sanjuán et al., 2004; Weinreich et al., 2006), and combinations of both (Sanjuán et al., 2005; Poon and Chao, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant studies.

claim: Studies of epistasis involve engineered site-directed mutations.
source: These and similar studies involve the analysis of standing genetic variation or spontaneous mutations (Bonhoeffer et al., 2004; Bershtein et al., 2006), engineered site-directed mutations (Sanjuán et al., 2004; Weinreich et al., 2006), and combinations of both (Sanjuán et al., 2005; Poon and Chao, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant studies.

claim: Competition experiments are frequently employed to learn mutational fitness effects.
source: Competition experiments are also frequently employed to learn mutational fitness effects.
evidence: This is a statement about common experimental practices.

claim: Sanjuán et al. (2004) studied the distribution of deleterious mutational effects in RNA viruses using competition experiments.
source: For example, Sanjuán et al. (2004) studied the distribution of deleterious mutational effects in RNA viruses using this approach.
evidence: This is supported by citation to the referenced study.

claim: Competition experiments are typically run on single-nucleotide substitution mutants produced by site-directed mutagenesis.
source: Such experiments are typically run on single-nucleotide substitution mutants produced by site-directed mutagenesis.
evidence: This is a statement about common experimental practices.

claim: Data produced in competition experiments is informative about pairwise comparisons of genotypes with respect to their fitness.
source: The data produced in competition experiments is informative about pairwise comparisons of genotypes with respect to their fitness.
evidence: This is a statement about the nature of data from competition experiments.

claim: Little is known about whether it is possible to learn higher order genetic interactions from fitness comparison data.
source: However, little is known about whether or not it is possible to learn higher order genetic interactions from such fitness comparison data.
evidence: This identifies a gap in knowledge that the manuscript addresses.

claim: The number of possible interactions grows rapidly with the number of loci.
source: Due to the rapid growth of the number of possible interactions with the number of loci, all interactions can exhaustively be studied only for a small number of loci.
evidence: This is a mathematical fact about combinatorial growth.

claim: A complete study of only pairwise gene interactions at the human genome scale would require hundreds of millions of experiments.
source: At the human genome scale, for example, a complete study of only pairwise gene interactions would already require hundreds of millions of experiments.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the number of gene pairs in the human genome.

claim: All pairwise and several three-way gene interactions have been measured experimentally in yeast.
source: On the other hand, for smaller organisms, such as yeast, all pairwise and several three-way gene interactions have been measured experimentally (Costanzo et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the referenced study.

claim: All combinations of mutations and epistatic interactions can be assessed only when restricting to a small set of preselected loci.
source: Only when restricting to a small set of preselected loci, can one assess all combinations of mutations and hence all epistatic interactions.
evidence: This is a statement about practical limitations in experimental design.

claim: Weinreich et al. (2006) assessed all combinations for a five-locus system associated with bacterial drug resistance.
source: This approach has been pursued, for example, by Weinreich et al. (2006) for a five-locus system associated with bacterial drug resistance.
evidence: This is supported by citation to the referenced study.

claim: Historically, the study of genetic interactions was mostly restricted to pairwise epistasis.
source: Historically, the study of genetic interactions was mostly restricted to pairwise epistasis.
evidence: This is a statement about the history of the field.

claim: According to Crow and Kimura (1970), higher order interactions were generally believed not to be significant in nature.
source: According to Crow and Kimura, 1970 (p. 224) higher order interactions were generally believed not to be significant in nature, with references to Fisher, Haldane, and Wright.
evidence: This is supported by citation to historical literature.

claim: More recent arguments suggest higher order interactions are not significant in the context of protein folding.
source: More recent arguments for the same view have been stated in the context of protein folding (Gupta and Adami, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to recent literature.

claim: Empirical findings suggest that higher order interactions are significant for many systems.
source: On the other hand, empirical findings suggest that the opposite is true for many other systems (Szendro et al., 2013; Neidhart et al., 2013; Sailer and Harms, 2017a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to empirical studies.

claim: Weinreich et al. (2013) argue that three-way and four-way interactions can be as strong as pairwise epistasis.
source: For example, Weinreich et al. (2013) argue that three-way and four-way interactions can be as strong as pairwise epistasis referring to various empirical fitness studies, and Knies et al. (2017) find many epistatic interactions in a numerically near-additive fitness landscape, reducing dramatically the number of accessible evolutionary trajectories.
evidence: This is supported by citation to the referenced study.

claim: Knies et al. (2017) find many epistatic interactions in a numerically near-additive fitness landscape.
source: For example, Weinreich et al. (2013) argue that three-way and four-way interactions can be as strong as pairwise epistasis referring to various empirical fitness studies, and Knies et al. (2017) find many epistatic interactions in a numerically near-additive fitness landscape, reducing dramatically the number of accessible evolutionary trajectories.
evidence: This is supported by citation to the referenced study.

claim: Epistatic interactions reduce dramatically the number of accessible evolutionary trajectories in near-additive fitness landscapes.
source: For example, Weinreich et al. (2013) argue that three-way and four-way interactions can be as strong as pairwise epistasis referring to various empirical fitness studies, and Knies et al. (2017) find many epistatic interactions in a numerically near-additive fitness landscape, reducing dramatically the number of accessible evolutionary trajectories.
evidence: This is a finding from the cited study.

claim: The significance of higher order interactions may vary between systems.
source: Although the significance of higher order interactions may vary between systems, the topic has not been thoroughly investigated.
evidence: This is a statement acknowledging variability and gaps in knowledge.

claim: The topic of higher order interactions has not been thoroughly investigated.
source: Although the significance of higher order interactions may vary between systems, the topic has not been thoroughly investigated.
evidence: This identifies a gap in the literature.

claim: Lack of adequate methodology to quantitatively assess interactions is partly responsible for insufficient investigation of higher order interactions.
source: This is partly due to lack of adequate methodology to quantitatively assess the interactions underlying an observed empirical fitness landscape.
evidence: This is an inference about the reasons for the gap in knowledge.

claim: Improved mathematical and statistical tools for detecting higher order interactions are necessary for more conclusive answers.
source: Improved mathematical and statistical tools for detecting higher order interactions, as well as more empirical results, are necessary for more conclusive answers regarding the importance of higher order interactions.
evidence: This is a statement about what is needed to advance the field.

claim: The paper considers fitness data that comes in the form of pairwise comparisons.
source: In this paper, we consider fitness data that comes in the form of pairwise comparisons.
evidence: This describes the type of data analyzed in the study.

claim: Pairwise comparison data are frequent in practice.
source: Such data are frequent in practice and can arise in different ways.
evidence: This is a statement about the prevalence of this type of data.

claim: Some assays rely on comparing the fitness of two genotypes by letting them grow in direct competition.
source: First, some assays rely on comparing the fitness of two genotypes, for example, by letting them grow in direct competition.
evidence: This describes a common experimental approach.

claim: Each competition experiment is informative about which of the two genotypes has higher fitness, without estimating the fitness values themselves.
source: Each competition experiment is informative about which of the two genotypes has higher fitness, without estimating the fitness values themselves.
evidence: This describes the nature of information from competition experiments.

claim: Direct but uncertain fitness measurements are often summarized as pairwise fitness relations by recording only whether two genotypes displayed significantly different fitness values or not.
source: Second, direct but uncertain fitness measurements are also often summarized as pairwise fitness relations by recording only whether two genotypes displayed significantly different fitness values or not.
evidence: This describes a common practice in data analysis.

claim: Fitness proxies generally do not preserve fitness linearity.
source: Fitness proxies cannot be used directly to measure epistasis, because they generally do not preserve fitness linearity (Gong et al., 2013), but if proxy data preserves pairwise comparisons, they may be used instead.
evidence: This is supported by citation to relevant literature.

claim: If proxy data preserves pairwise comparisons, they may be used for epistasis analysis.
source: Fitness proxies cannot be used directly to measure epistasis, because they generally do not preserve fitness linearity (Gong et al., 2013), but if proxy data preserves pairwise comparisons, they may be used instead.
evidence: This is an inference about when proxy data can be useful.

claim: Lists of mutants found in a new environment can be utilized to provide pairwise fitness comparisons.
source: Lists of mutants found in a new environment, such as, for example, a new host for a pathogen or a drug environment can be utilized similarly.
evidence: This describes how observational data can be used.

claim: The capability to transition to and survive in a new environment is an indication of higher fitness.
source: Assuming that the capability to transition to and survive in the new environment is an indication of higher fitness, this type of observational data also provides pairwise fitness comparisons.
evidence: This is an assumption used to interpret observational data.

claim: Population frequency of genotypes can sometimes be used to draw conclusions about fitness.
source: Similarly, the population frequency of genotypes can sometimes be used to draw conclusions about fitness.
evidence: This describes another way to infer fitness information.

claim: Fitness was inferred computationally from deep sequencing data of an HIV-1 population using a specific model of viral evolution.
source: For example, by employing a specific model of viral evolution, fitness was inferred computationally from deep sequencing data of an HIV-1 population, and pairwise credible fitness differences were reported (Seifert et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the referenced study.

claim: Any consistent set of pairwise fitness relations can be regarded as a partial order of the genotypes with respect to fitness.
source: Irrespective of how they were obtained, any consistent set of pairwise fitness relations can be regarded as a partial order of the genotypes with respect to fitness.
evidence: This is a mathematical statement about how to represent pairwise comparisons.

claim: If comparisons are available for all pairs of genotypes, then the partial order is a total order, or rank order.
source: First, if comparisons are available for all pairs of genotypes, then the partial order is a total order, or rank order.
evidence: This is a definition from order theory.

claim: Fitness graphs are partial orders where fitness is compared only between mutational neighbors.
source: Second, several studies compare fitness only between mutational neighbors, that is, genotypes which differ at exactly one locus. The resulting partial orders are referred to as fitness graphs and have recently been used extensively (Ogbunugafor et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2016; Smith and Cobey, 2016; Mira et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a definition supported by citations to studies using fitness graphs.

claim: Connections between rank orders and fitness graphs to epistasis have been observed repeatedly.
source: Connections between rank orders and fitness graphs to epistasis and global properties of fitness landscapes have been observed repeatedly (Greene and Crona, 2014; Crona et al., 2013; Poelwijk et al., 2011; Weinreich et al., 2006; Weinreich et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Wu et al. (2016) discussed an example of a fitness graph that implies higher order epistasis.
source: Most recently, Wu et al. (2016) discussed an example of a fitness graph that implies higher order epistasis.
evidence: This is supported by citation to the referenced study.

claim: The significance of rank orders of genotypes for epistasis was recognized by Weinreich et al. (2005).
source: The significance of rank orders of genotypes for epistasis was recognized by Weinreich et al. (2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the referenced study.

claim: Weinreich et al. (2005) introduced the concept of sign epistasis.
source: The authors introduced the concept of sign epistasis.
evidence: This is supported by citation to the referenced study.

claim: A system has sign epistasis if the sign of the effect of a mutation depends on genetic background.
source: By definition, a system has sign epistasis if the sign of the effect of a mutation, whether positive or negative, depends on genetic background.
evidence: This is a definition from the cited work.

claim: Sign epistasis implies that the rank order of the genotypes is not compatible with additive fitness.
source: Importantly, sign epistasis implies that the rank order of the genotypes is not compatible with additive fitness.
evidence: This is a theoretical result about sign epistasis.

claim: The paper develops an approach based on rank orders that applies to higher order epistasis and other measures of gene interactions.
source: In this paper, we develop a related approach based on rank orders that applies to higher order epistasis as well as other measures of gene interactions.
evidence: This describes the contribution of the manuscript.

claim: If the rank order of the genotypes implies three-way epistasis for a three-locus system, then one has a signed variant of three-way epistasis.
source: For instance, if the rank order of the genotypes implies three-way epistasis for a three-locus system, then one has a signed variant of three-way epistasis.
evidence: This is a theoretical concept introduced in the manuscript.

claim: Signed variants can be considered for almost any type of gene interaction.
source: Similarly, one can consider signed variants of almost any type of gene interaction.
evidence: This is a generalization of the approach.

claim: The theory of sign epistasis stands as a model for development in the area.
source: The theory of sign epistasis stands as a model for development in the area, and there is a potential for understanding global properties of fitness landscapes in terms of (local) signed interactions, similar to results for sign epistasis.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential of the approach.

claim: Rank order arguments have been used for developing antimicrobial treatment strategies.
source: In addition to the theoretical work mentioned above, rank order arguments have been used for developing antimicrobial treatment strategies (Smith and Cobey, 2016; Nichol et al., 2015; Mira et al., 2015; Goulart et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant studies.

claim: The general case of arbitrary partial fitness orders has not been considered before.
source: Furthermore, to the best of our knowledge the general case of arbitrary partial fitness orders has yet to be considered.
evidence: This identifies a gap that the manuscript addresses.

claim: The paper develops quantitative tools to detect any type of gene interactions measured by linear forms.
source: Here, we develop quantitative tools to detect any type of gene interactions measured by linear forms, including epistasis as described by Fourier coefficients, Walsh coefficients, and circuits (Beerenwinkel et al., 2007; Weinreich et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes the contribution of the manuscript.

claim: Higher order interactions were detected in all analyzed systems based only on partial information about the fitness order of genotypes.
source: In all cases, we detect higher order interactions based only on partial information about the fitness order of genotypes, without knowing or estimating the actual fitness values.
evidence: This is a summary of the empirical findings.

claim: Fitness is assumed to be additive in the absence of epistasis.
source: We assume that fitness is additive in the absence of epistasis.
evidence: This is a theoretical assumption.

claim: This level of completeness is rarely available in empirical data sets due to experimental design or an infeasible number of genotypes.
source: However, this level of completeness is rarely available in empirical data sets due to experimental design or an infeasible number of genotypes.
evidence: This is a statement about practical limitations.

claim: Methods were developed that are applicable to partial orders of genotypes according to fitness.
source: To address this limitation, we developed methods that are applicable to partial orders of genotypes according to fitness.
evidence: This describes the methodological contribution.

claim: One can always extend a partial order to a rank order.
source: One can always extend a partial order to a rank order, that is, a total order of the genotypes in the system from highest to lowest fitness.
evidence: This is a mathematical fact from order theory.

claim: The rank order alone allows one to detect positive epistasis without knowledge of the actual fitness values.
source: It follows that the rank order alone allows one to detect positive epistasis without knowledge of the actual fitness values.
evidence: This is a key finding of the theoretical analysis.

claim: There are 24 rank orders of the biallelic two-locus system.
source: There are 24 rank orders of the biallelic two-locus system.
evidence: This is a combinatorial calculation.

claim: Among the 24 rank orders, eight imply positive epistasis, eight imply negative epistasis, and eight do not permit any inference regarding epistasis.
source: Among these, eight imply positive epistasis, eight imply negative epistasis, and eight do not permit any inference regarding epistasis.
evidence: This is a result from enumerating all possibilities.

claim: Two thirds of the rank orders imply epistasis for the two-locus system.
source: In total two thirds of the rank orders imply epistasis.
evidence: This is calculated from the enumeration.

claim: There are six rank orders that extend the partial order w₀₁>w₀₀ and w₁₀>w₁₁.
source: There are six such total extensions, namely rank orders 9, 10, 12, 13, 14, and 16 in Figure 1, and all imply negative epistasis.
evidence: This is determined by enumerating extensions of the partial order.

claim: If all total extensions of a partial order imply epistasis then the partial order itself implies epistasis.
source: If all total extensions imply epistasis then the same is true for the partial order.
evidence: This is a general principle used in the analysis.

claim: Fitness graphs constitute an important subclass of partial orders.
source: Fitness graphs constitute an important subclass of partial orders, as they often are the reported result of experiments, and because of their relevance for evolutionary processes (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a statement about the importance of fitness graphs.

claim: The nodes of a fitness graph represent genotypes.
source: Briefly, the nodes of a fitness graph represent genotypes and for each pair of mutational neighbors, that is, genotypes which differ at exactly one locus, an arrow points toward the genotype of higher fitness (Section Partial orders and fitness graphs).
evidence: This is a definition of fitness graphs.

claim: A fitness graph implies epistasis exactly when all rank orders compatible with the graph do.
source: A fitness graph implies epistasis exactly when all rank orders compatible with the graph do, as is the case for partial orders in general.
evidence: This is a theoretical result about fitness graphs.

claim: Fitness graphs (b), (c) and (d) in Figure 3 imply epistasis, whereas (a) is compatible with additive fitness.
source: The graphs (b), (c) and (d) imply epistasis, whereas (a) is compatible with additive fitness.
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: Some rank orders imply three-way epistasis.
source: Some rank orders imply three-way epistasis, similar to our observation of epistasis in the two-locus case.
evidence: This is a finding from the theoretical analysis.

claim: A single quantity cannot capture all possible gene interactions.
source: However, a single quantity cannot capture all possible gene interactions.
evidence: This is a statement about the complexity of gene interactions.

claim: Rank order approaches have the capacity to reveal finer interactions.
source: Rank order approaches have the capacity to reveal finer interactions as well.
evidence: This is a claim about the power of the method.

claim: Interaction coordinates and circuits are additive dependence relations.
source: Interaction coordinates and circuits (Beerenwinkel et al., 2007), as well as Walsh coefficients of order two or more (Weinreich et al., 2013), are additive dependence relations.
evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: Walsh coefficients of order two or more are additive dependence relations.
source: Interaction coordinates and circuits (Beerenwinkel et al., 2007), as well as Walsh coefficients of order two or more (Weinreich et al., 2013), are additive dependence relations.
evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: If a rank order implies that the sign of an additive dependence relation is determined, then the system has sign epistasis.
source: Importantly, if a rank order implies that the sign of an additive dependence relation, such as a circuit or an interaction coordinates, is determined, then the system has sign epistasis.
evidence: This is a theoretical result connecting rank orders to sign epistasis.

claim: The most computationally demanding task of the algorithms is reading the rank order from disk.
source: The most computationally demanding task of our algorithms is reading the rank order from disk.
evidence: This is a statement about the computational complexity.

claim: The run time complexity is proportional to the number of non-zero coefficients in the linear form.
source: The run time complexity is proportional to the number of non-zero coefficients in the linear form.
evidence: This is a statement about the computational complexity.

claim: The approach reveals higher order epistasis for HIV-1, malaria, antibiotic resistance, and Aspergillus Niger systems.
source: As proof of principle, we applied our tools to fitness data from a diverse set of biological systems, ranging from HIV-1 (Segal et al., 2004), malaria (Ogbunugafor and Hartl, 2016), antibiotic resistance (Mira et al., 2015), to the fungus Aspergillus Niger (Franke et al., 2011). Our approach reveals higher order epistasis for all of these systems, only by considering rank orders and partial orders of genotypes, without the need to access direct fitness measurements or estimates.
evidence: This is a summary of the empirical applications.

claim: Fitness was measured as the number of offspring in a single replication cycle of the virus in the HIV-1 study.
source: Fitness was measured as the number of offspring in a single replication cycle of the virus in the original study, and was reported relative to the wild-type strain NL4-3 on a logarithmic scale.
evidence: This describes the fitness measurement method in the cited study.

claim: The three mutations under consideration in HIV-1 together have a stronger effect on fitness than predicted from single and double mutants.
source: It follows that the three mutations under consideration together have a stronger effect on fitness than one would predict from single and double mutants.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the positive three-way epistasis finding.

claim: The rank order approach required much less information to arrive at the same conclusions as conventional methods for HIV-1.
source: We emphasize that the rank order approach required much less information to arrive at the same conclusions, thus demonstrating the power of the method.
evidence: This is a comparison of the efficiency of different methods.

claim: The three sites in the HIV-1 genome under consideration are prone to a diverse set of interactions.
source: We conclude that the three sites in the HIV-1 genome under consideration are prone to a diverse set of interactions.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the analysis of HIV-1 data.

claim: Higher order interactions have a strong impact on the HIV-1 fitness landscape.
source: Thus, in this data set, higher order interactions have a strong impact on the fitness landscape.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the analysis of HIV-1 data.

claim: The malaria study measured growth rates for several mutants of Plasmodium vivax under exposure to pyrimethamine.
source: The authors measured growth rates for several mutants of Plasmodium vivax under exposure to the antimalarial drug pyrimethamine.
evidence: This describes the data from the cited study.

claim: Higher order epistasis was identified in malaria by analyzing rank orders.
source: We identified higher order epistasis by analyzing rank orders.
evidence: This is a finding from applying the method to malaria data.

claim: The malaria analysis considered a three-locus sub-system consisting of mutations N50I, S58R, and S117N, in the context of T173L.
source: More precisely, we considered a three-locus sub-system of the study that consists of mutations N50I, S58R, and S117N, in the context of T173L, a fixed mutation, under nine different concentrations of pyrimethamine.
evidence: This describes the specific system analyzed.

claim: The malaria system has negative three-way epistasis for the three highest concentrations of pyrimethamine.
source: Since we obtain Dyck words in all cases, the system has negative three-way epistasis for the three highest concentrations of the drug.
evidence: This is a finding from applying the method to malaria data.

claim: The consistency of negative three-way epistasis among pyrimethamine concentrations shows that the result is robust.
source: This consistency among pyrimethamine concentrations shows that the result is robust.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the consistency across conditions.

claim: The fitness graph for TEM-family under FEP Cefepime exposure implies higher order epistasis.
source: The fitness graph implies higher order epistasis (Proposition 7), that is, the fitness of TEM-50 cannot be predicted even with complete knowledge of the fitness values of the remaining genotypes in the system.
evidence: This is a finding from applying the method to TEM-family data.

claim: The fitness graphs for the other 14 antibiotics in the TEM-family study do not imply higher order epistasis.
source: The fitness graphs for the other 14 antibiotics do not share this property.
evidence: This is a finding from analyzing the TEM-family data.

claim: A large population of triple mutants in TEM-family is more prone to become antibiotic resistant due to the epistatic fitness advantage of TEM-50.
source: We conclude that even though some of the single and triple mutants confer low antibiotic resistance, a large population of triple mutants alone is more prone to become antibiotic resistant due to the epistatic fitness advantage of TEM-50, as compared to a setting with no higher order epistasis.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the higher order epistasis finding.

claim: The Aspergillus Niger study considered a system consisting of the wild type and all combinations of four individually deleterious mutations.
source: We considered a system consisting of the wild type and all combinations of the four individually deleterious mutations fwnA1, leuA1, oliC2 and crnB12 (Figure 9).
evidence: This describes the system analyzed from the cited study.

claim: Fitness in the Aspergillus Niger study was estimated with two-fold replication by measuring the linear mycelium growth rate.
source: Fitness was estimated with two-fold replication by measuring the linear mycelium growth rate in the original study.
evidence: This describes the fitness measurement method in the cited study.

claim: The fitness graph for Aspergillus Niger implies higher order epistasis.
source: The fitness graph implies higher order epistasis (Proposition 7).
evidence: This is a finding from applying the method to Aspergillus Niger data.

claim: An additive fitness landscape is single peaked.
source: In contrast, an additive fitness landscape is single peaked.
evidence: This is a known property of additive landscapes.

claim: Epistasis may have an impact on the evolutionary dynamics.
source: This example illustrates that epistasis may have an impact on the evolutionary dynamics.
evidence: This is an inference from the analysis of the Aspergillus Niger system.

claim: Several peaks can make the evolutionary process less predictable.
source: Several peaks can make the evolutionary process less predictable, depending also on other factors such as population size, mutation rate, etc.
evidence: This is a statement about evolutionary dynamics.

claim: Higher order epistasis correlates with more peaks in three-locus fitness graphs.
source: We found that higher order epistasis correlates with more peaks as well as other features that can lead to involved evolutionary dynamics (Mathematical framework and proofs, Section Graph theoretical aspects).
evidence: This is a finding from systematic analysis of three-locus fitness graphs.

claim: Gene interactions play a critical role in evolutionary processes.
source: Gene interactions play a critical role in evolutionary processes.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in evolutionary biology.

claim: Important features of fitness landscapes depend on epistatic gene interactions.
source: Important features of fitness landscapes, such as the number of peaks, and accessible evolutionary trajectories, depend on epistatic gene interactions.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in evolutionary biology.

claim: The importance of higher order versus pairwise epistasis remains a central research topic.
source: The importance of higher order versus pairwise epistasis, within and among genes or in non-coding regions, as well as the impact of higher order epistasis on evolutionary dynamics, remains a central research topic (Sailer and Harms, 2017b; Wu et al., 2016; Weinreich et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: Progress in understanding gene interactions requires adequate mathematical and statistical approaches, in addition to empirical studies.
source: Progress in all of these areas requires adequate mathematical and statistical approaches, in addition to empirical studies.
evidence: This is a statement about what is needed to advance the field.

claim: The main advantage of the tools is that they can reveal gene interactions from types of data frequently generated in empirical studies.
source: The main advantage of our tools is that they can reveal gene interactions from the types of data frequently generated in empirical studies, specifically rank orders, fitness graphs, and general partial orders of genotypes.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the methods.

claim: Reasons for availability of partial order data include restricted comparative experimental designs and confounding factors in measuring fitness.
source: The reasons why, in practice, these types of data are available more often than precise fitness measurements for each genotype are manifold. They include restricted comparative experimental designs and known and unknown confounding factors in measuring fitness that can result in uncertain and biased estimates.
evidence: This is a statement about practical limitations in empirical research.

claim: The methods allow for studying epistatic interactions even when direct fitness measurements are lacking or only a subset of pairwise fitness comparisons is available.
source: The methods presented here allow for studying epistatic interactions even when direct fitness measurements are lacking or only a subset of pairwise fitness comparisons is available, either as the immediate outcome of the experiment or the reported summary.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the methods.

claim: A complete characterization of rank orders that imply higher order epistasis is provided.
source: We provide a complete characterization of rank orders that imply higher order epistasis, along with precise results for fitness graphs of three-locus systems.
evidence: This is a summary of the theoretical contribution.

claim: The approach applies to general partial orders.
source: In principle, our approach applies to general partial orders as well, and we have implemented algorithms accordingly.
evidence: This is a statement about the generality of the approach.

claim: It would be desirable to have theoretical results for handling large systems due to increasing computational complexity.
source: However, because of the increasing computational complexity it would be desirable to have theoretical results for handling large systems.
evidence: This is a statement about future directions.

claim: A characterization of fitness graphs that imply higher order epistasis is of independent mathematical interest.
source: In particular, a characterization of fitness graphs that imply higher order epistasis is of independent mathematical interest.
evidence: This is a statement about an open problem.

claim: For biallelic three-locus systems, 40% of all possible rank orders imply higher order epistasis.
source: We found that for biallelic three-locus systems, 40% of all possible rank orders and 37% of all possible fitness graphs imply higher order epistasis.
evidence: This is a finding from the theoretical analysis.

claim: For biallelic three-locus systems, 37% of all possible fitness graphs imply higher order epistasis.
source: We found that for biallelic three-locus systems, 40% of all possible rank orders and 37% of all possible fitness graphs imply higher order epistasis.
evidence: This is a finding from the theoretical analysis.

claim: These fractions suggest that the methods have a good capacity to detect higher order epistasis among three loci.
source: These fractions suggest that our methods have a good capacity to detect higher order epistasis among three loci, even if exact and complete fitness measurements or estimates are not available.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the theoretical results.

claim: Many rank orders are informative regarding other additive dependence relations, such as circuits measuring conditional epistasis.
source: However, many rank orders are informative regarding other additive dependence relations, for instance some circuits measuring conditional epistasis.
evidence: This is a finding from the theoretical analysis.

claim: The power of the methods was demonstrated for a diverse set of biological systems.
source: Moreover, the power of our methods was demonstrated for a diverse set of biological systems.
evidence: This is a summary of the empirical applications.

claim: The findings suggest that genetic interactions beyond two-way epistasis shape the fitness landscapes of the analyzed genetic systems.
source: Our findings suggest that genetic interactions beyond two-way epistasis shape the fitness landscapes of these genetic systems and may play an important role in determining their evolutionary trajectories.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the empirical findings.

claim: Various types of higher order interactions were exhaustively investigated in HIV-1.
source: We also exhaustively investigated various types of higher order interactions in HIV-1 and discovered a complex pattern of interactions, confirming that our approach is powerful enough to detect finer gene interactions.
evidence: This is a summary of the HIV-1 analysis.

claim: Over twenty interactions were identified by conventional approaches in HIV-1, and rank order methods detected about half of them.
source: Specifically, we identified over twenty interactions by conventional approaches, and rank order methods detected about half of them.
evidence: This compares the rank order method to conventional approaches.

claim: The method allows for prioritizing further experiments by suggesting additional comparisons of genotypes.
source: Another important application of our method is to experimental design. When the information available in the data does not contradict an interaction, but is not conclusive enough to claim the interaction, for example because the number of performed competition experiments is too small, then the method allows for prioritizing further experiments by suggesting additional comparisons of genotypes.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the method for experimental design.

claim: This feature may prove useful in guiding fitness experiments that aim for testing specific interactions and allow for iteration.
source: This feature may prove useful in guiding fitness experiments that aim for testing specific interactions and allow for iteration.
evidence: This is a statement about potential applications.

claim: Genetic interactions, especially those of higher order, are particularly difficult to detect in high-dimensional systems.
source: Genetic interactions, especially those of higher order, are particularly difficult to detect in high-dimensional systems, where complete fitness measurements of all genotypes are infeasible.
evidence: This is a statement about challenges in the field.

claim: Human genome-wide association studies (GWAS) are a prime example of high-dimensional systems.
source: Human genome-wide association studies (GWAS) are a prime example.
evidence: This is a statement about a specific application area.

claim: Most diseases are polygenic, rather than monogenic.
source: Since most diseases are polygenic, rather than monogenic, genetic interactions play an important role, and accounting for them may explain some of the missing heritability and improve genetic disease models.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in genetics.

claim: Accounting for genetic interactions may explain some of the missing heritability and improve genetic disease models.
source: Since most diseases are polygenic, rather than monogenic, genetic interactions play an important role, and accounting for them may explain some of the missing heritability and improve genetic disease models.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential importance of considering interactions.

claim: Several methods have been proposed for detecting pairwise interactions in GWAS.
source: Several methods have been proposed for detecting pairwise interactions in GWAS, most of them relying on scanning all or a prioritized subset of pairs of loci (Wei et al., 2014), but little is known about higher order interactions in these landscapes.
evidence: This is supported by citation to relevant literature.

claim: Little is known about higher order interactions in GWAS landscapes.
source: Several methods have been proposed for detecting pairwise interactions in GWAS, most of them relying on scanning all or a prioritized subset of pairs of loci (Wei et al., 2014), but little is known about higher order interactions in these landscapes.
evidence: This identifies a gap in knowledge.

claim: The methods may help address the challenge of detecting higher order interactions in GWAS.
source: The methods presented in the present study may help addressing this challenge as they can sometimes reveal higher order interactions from a small number of comparisons, and the choice of genotypes to compare can be optimized if particular interactions are to be tested.
evidence: This is a statement about potential applications.

claim: Another advantage is the flexibility of the approach regarding the type of epistatic interaction analyzed.
source: Another advantage is the flexibility of our approach regarding the type of epistatic interaction analyzed.
evidence: This is a statement about the generality of the approach.

claim: Huggins et al. (2007) explored circuits and their sign patterns for genotype data from the HapMap project in two ENCODE regions.
source: Towards this end, Huggins et al. (2007) have explored circuits and their sign patterns for genotype data from the HapMap project in two ENCODE regions.
evidence: This is supported by citation to the referenced study.

claim: The Dyck word approach will be particularly useful if quantitative data on the phenotype is difficult to obtain, but rank order information is more accessible.
source: The Dyck word approach will be particularly useful if quantitative data on the phenotype is difficult to obtain, but rank order information is more accessible, for example by considering disease indicators, rather than the condition itself.
evidence: This is a statement about when the approach is most useful.

claim: There is a distinction between rank order-induced gene interactions and interactions that do not change the rank order of genotypes.
source: For a more theoretical perspective, we emphasize the distinction between rank order-induced gene interactions, and interactions that do not change the rank order of genotypes.
evidence: This is a conceptual distinction made in the manuscript.

claim: Rank order-induced gene interactions of any type can be regarded as analogues to sign epistasis.
source: Rank order-induced gene interactions of any type can thus be regarded as analogues to sign epistasis.
evidence: This is a conceptual connection made in the manuscript.

claim: There exist a number of possible ways to quantify and interpret higher order interactions.
source: There exist a number of possible ways to quantify and interpret higher order interactions (Weinreich et al., 2013; Beerenwinkel et al., 2007; Hallgrímsdóttir and Yuster, 2008), and our rank order approach applies to any type of gene interactions measured by linear forms.
evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: The rank order approach can detect interactions as described by Fourier coefficients and Walsh coefficients.
source: In particular, we can detect interactions as described by Fourier coefficients and Walsh coefficients.
evidence: This is a statement about the scope of the approach.

claim: Further investigation of rank order-induced interaction has the potential to relate global and local properties of fitness landscapes.
source: Further investigation of rank order-induced interaction has the potential to relate global and local properties of fitness landscapes, similarly to results on sign epistasis (Weinreich et al., 2005; Poelwijk et al., 2011; Crona et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a statement about future directions supported by citations.

claim: Global properties concern peaks and mutational trajectories in the fitness landscape.
source: Global properties concern peaks and mutational trajectories in the fitness landscape, whereas local properties concern, for instance, fitness graphs for small system.
evidence: This is a definition of terms used in the discussion.

claim: Local properties concern fitness graphs for small systems.
source: Global properties concern peaks and mutational trajectories in the fitness landscape, whereas local properties concern, for instance, fitness graphs for small system.
evidence: This is a definition of terms used in the discussion.

claim: The relation between global and local properties is important since only local properties can be easily observed in experiments or nature.
source: The relation between global and local properties is important since only local properties can be easily observed in experiments or nature.
evidence: This is a statement about the practical importance of understanding this relationship.

claim: One can identify or rule out sign epistasis in a system from inspection of two-locus subsystems only.
source: A very useful feature of sign epistasis is that one can identify, or rule out, sign epistasis in a system from inspection of two-locus subsystems only.
evidence: This is a known property of sign epistasis.

claim: The theoretical significance and applicability of sign epistasis depends on its local nature.
source: The theoretical significance and applicability of sign epistasis depends on its local nature.
evidence: This is a statement about why sign epistasis is useful.

claim: The signed versions of other gene interactions are sometimes local as well.
source: Fortunately, the signed versions of other gene interactions are sometimes local as well.
evidence: This is a finding from the theoretical analysis.

claim: It seems plausible that the absence of rank order induced conditional epistasis of specified orders correlates with few peaks and good peak accessibility.
source: For instance, it seems plausible that the absence of rank order induced conditional epistasis of specified orders (a local property) correlates with few peaks and good peak accessibility.
evidence: This is a speculation about relationships between properties.

claim: Theory for sign epistasis stands as a model for further development in this area.
source: Theory for sign epistasis stands as a model for further development in this area.
evidence: This is a statement about future directions.

claim: The method has been applied only to fitness in this manuscript, but any other continuous phenotype of interest can be analyzed in exactly the same manner.
source: Although we have applied our method here only to fitness, any other continuous phenotype of interest can be analyzed in exactly the same manner.
evidence: This is a statement about the generality of the approach.

claim: One may be concerned about the drug resistance phenotype itself and its genetic architecture rather than using it as a fitness proxy.
source: For example, rather than using it as a fitness proxy, one may be concerned about the drug resistance phenotype itself and its genetic architecture.
evidence: This is an example of an alternative application.

claim: Rank order methods have potential for the interpretation of empirical data.
source: In summary, rank order methods have potential for the interpretation of empirical data, as well as for relating higher order gene interactions and evolutionary dynamics.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the utility of the methods.

claim: Rank order methods have potential for relating higher order gene interactions and evolutionary dynamics.
source: In summary, rank order methods have potential for the interpretation of empirical data, as well as for relating higher order gene interactions and evolutionary dynamics.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the utility of the methods.

claim: The approach facilitates detecting higher order epistasis from a very broad range of empirical data.
source: Our approach facilitates detecting higher order epistasis from a very broad range of empirical data, and will therefore contribute to enhancing our general understanding of empirical fitness landscapes and epistatic gene interactions.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the contribution of the work.
